title: No thief of the will
hookLine: Marcus quotes Epictetus: no one can rob us of our will (Meditations 11.36)

lines: LIFE HAS A LOT OF THIEVES.
cards: Someone steals your bike. Someone takes credit for your idea. Someone cuts your hours, or your budget, or your part in the school play.
Life has a lot of thieves. Toward the end of book eleven, Marcus stops writing his own thoughts for a while and copies out a string of sayings from Epictetus, the teacher who had once been enslaved.
One is only a few words long, and it names the one thing no thief can take.

teach.b: First, who's speaking. Epictetus was born into slavery, studied philosophy, and later taught it as a free man in Greece. As far as we know, Marcus never met him.
But in book one Marcus thanks his teacher Rusticus for lending him Epictetus's discourses from his own library.
Near the end of book eleven, Marcus writes out several Epictetus lines in a row, like favorite quotations copied into a notebook. Second, the line. A thief of the will, Marcus quotes, doesn't exist.
No one can rob you of your choice. Third, the word. The Greek is prohairesis: the power to choose, to decide what you'll agree to, what you'll want, what you'll do.
For Epictetus it's the one thing that truly belongs to you.

teach.h: NO ONE CAN ROB YOUR CHOICE.
teach.b: Your body, your possessions, your reputation, your job can all be taken.
Your choice about how to meet the loss can't be. Fourth, what it doesn't mean. It doesn't mean nothing hurts, or that circumstances don't matter.
A person in prison has fewer choices than a person on a beach, and Epictetus knew that better than most.
But even inside narrow walls, he taught, there's still the choice of how you stand there.
That small, steady choice is what no one can steal.

how: Readers of Epictetus and Marcus often respond to a loss by naming what remains in their control, their response, and making one deliberate choice about it.

games.q: you've lost a job you loved. you're Epictetus, who was once enslaved. what can't be taken?
o: your choice about how to meet this.
games.why: no one can rob us of our will, says the line Marcus copied. the body, the job, the reputation can be taken; the choice can't.

practice: Think of something that's been taken from you, small or large, time, a plan, a person's trust, and let yourself feel the loss honestly. Then look for what wasn't taken: your choice about how to respond, right now.
Hold that one choice; nobody handed it to you, and nobody can take it.

wordCard.voice: Epictetus. Born into slavery, he taught that a thief of the will doesn't exist, and Marcus copied his line into book eleven. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: choice, will, the power to decide. Epictetus's word for what is truly ours.

carryVoice: Your line: no thief. The loss is real, and so is the choice that stays. That's day six hundred twenty-seven.
